<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"

         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
    <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
    <version>0.1.5</version>
    <packaging>pom</packaging>

    <name>Pathland Java</name>
    <description>
        Framework-agnostic JVM libraries for the Pathland UI protocol: a Kotlin
        authoring DSL with Angular-style signals/computed/effects, a Kotlin opcode
        engine/SPI, the wire codec, JNA ring interop, a reusable HTML renderer, and
        cross-platform state stores. Java hosts (Spring Boot, Quarkus, desktop) mount
        Kotlin-authored views. Runs on every LTS from Java 17.
    </description>

    <url>https://github.com/PathlandDev/Pathland</url>

    <licenses>
        <license>
            <name>Apache License, Version 2.0</name>
            <url>https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt</url>
            <distribution>repo</distribution>
        </license>
    </licenses>

    <developers>
        <developer>
            <id>michaelkrog</id>
            <name>Michael Krog</name>
            <email>mic@apaq.dk</email>
            <url>https://github.com/michaelkrog</url>
        </developer>
    </developers>

    <scm>
        <connection>scm:git:https://github.com/PathlandDev/Pathland.git</connection>
        <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/PathlandDev/Pathland.git</developerConnection>
        <url>https://github.com/PathlandDev/Pathland</url>
        <tag>HEAD</tag>
    </scm>

    <modules>
        <module>pathland-view-core</module>
        <module>pathland-demo-views-kotlin</module>
        <module>pathland-render-html</module>
        <module>pathland-server-core</module>
        <module>pathland-spring-boot-starter</module>
        <module>pathland-quarkus</module>
        <module>pathland-quarkus-deployment</module>
        <module>pathland-desktop-demo</module>
        <module>pathland-quarkus-demo</module>
        <module>pathland-spring-boot-demo</module>
    </modules>

    <properties>
        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
        <!-- Whole-stack floor: every LTS from Java 17. ScopedValue was replaced with a
             thread-local environment and the FFM ring interop with JNA to achieve this. -->
        <maven.compiler.release>17</maven.compiler.release>
        <kotlin.version>2.4.10</kotlin.version>
        <jna.version>5.14.0</jna.version>
        <quarkus.version>3.39.1</quarkus.version>
        <spring-boot.version>3.5.16</spring-boot.version>
        <junit.version>5.10.2</junit.version>
        <lettuce.version>6.4.1.RELEASE</lettuce.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencyManagement>
        <dependencies>
            <dependency>
                <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
                <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
                <version>${junit.version}</version>
                <scope>test</scope>
            </dependency>
            <dependency>
                <groupId>net.java.dev.jna</groupId>
                <artifactId>jna</artifactId>
                <version>${jna.version}</version>
            </dependency>
            <dependency>
                <groupId>io.lettuce</groupId>
                <artifactId>lettuce-core</artifactId>
                <version>${lettuce.version}</version>
            </dependency>
            <dependency>
                <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
                <artifactId>quarkus-bom</artifactId>
                <version>${quarkus.version}</version>
                <type>pom</type>
                <scope>import</scope>
            </dependency>
            <dependency>
                <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
                <artifactId>spring-boot-dependencies</artifactId>
                <version>${spring-boot.version}</version>
                <type>pom</type>
                <scope>import</scope>
            </dependency>
        </dependencies>
    </dependencyManagement>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <!-- The Java DSL and its integrations are removed: keep them out. -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-enforcer-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.5.0</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>ban-removed-java-dsl</id>
                        <goals><goal>enforce</goal></goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <rules>
                                <bannedDependencies>
                                    <excludes>
                                        <exclude>dev.pathland:pathland-view</exclude>
                                        <exclude>dev.pathland:pathland-view-processor</exclude>
                                        <exclude>dev.pathland:pathland-quarkus-java</exclude>
                                        <exclude>dev.pathland:pathland-quarkus-starter</exclude>
                                    </excludes>
                                </bannedDependencies>
                            </rules>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
        <pluginManagement>
            <plugins>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                    <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>3.2.5</version>
                </plugin>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                    <artifactId>maven-resources-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>3.3.1</version>
                    <configuration>
                        <!-- Re-copy static resources (e.g. the rebuilt
                             content-hashed dom-renderer bundle and its
                             dom-renderer.current manifest) over existing target
                             files instead of failing with FileAlreadyExistsException
                             on repeat builds. -->
                        <overwrite>true</overwrite>
                    </configuration>
                </plugin>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
                    <artifactId>quarkus-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>${quarkus.version}</version>
                </plugin>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
                    <artifactId>quarkus-extension-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>${quarkus.version}</version>
                </plugin>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                    <artifactId>maven-enforcer-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>3.5.0</version>
                </plugin>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
                    <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>${spring-boot.version}</version>
                </plugin>
            </plugins>
        </pluginManagement>
    </build>

    <!-- Run BEFORE an IntelliJ IDE run: refreshes the two layers the IDE cannot rebuild
         itself — the Rust cdylib (cargo) and the DOM bundle (npm build:all) — plus the
         render-html module's embedded dylib (its antrun embed step only runs under Maven,
         NOT under IntelliJ's own build). IntelliJ then compiles the Java modules from its
         module outputs (the pathland modules are imported, so no ~/.m2 is used) and copies
         the refreshed bundle + its dom-renderer.current manifest into target/classes on
         Build Project. Invoke with `mvn -P refresh-ide validate`, then Reload All Maven
         Projects → Build → Run → reload. The bundle is content-hashed
         (dom-renderer-<sha256>.js) so a rebuilt bundle busts the immutable asset cache by
         URL — a normal reload after restart is enough, no hard refresh. -->
    <profiles>
    <!-- Maven Central publishing (`mvn -P release deploy`). Normal builds/tests are
         unaffected: this profile only activates on demand. -->
    <profile>
        <id>release</id>
        <build>
            <plugins>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                    <artifactId>maven-source-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>3.3.1</version>
                    <executions>
                        <execution>
                            <id>attach-sources</id>
                            <goals><goal>jar-no-fork</goal></goals>
                        </execution>
                    </executions>
                </plugin>

# Releasing Pathland

Publishing a **GitHub Release** (tagged `vX.Y.Z`) runs
`.github/workflows/release.yml`, which sets the version from the tag, builds and
publishes every artifact, attaches the built files to the Release, and commits
the version back to `main`:

| Ecosystem | Artifacts | Registry |
|-----------|-----------|----------|
| Rust | `pathland-core`, `pathland-markdown`, `pathland-engine`, `pathland-view`, `pathland-core-transport`, `pathland-render-html` | crates.io |
| Java | `dev.pathland:*` libraries (pure JVM — the HTML renderer and Markdown parser are Java ports) | Maven Central |

## Versioning (tag-driven)

**The tag drives the version** — no pre-bump commit is needed:

- The workflow writes `X.Y.Z` (from the tag `vX.Y.Z`) into
  `lib/rust/Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.package] version` + the intra-workspace
  path-dep pins, via `cargo set-version --workspace`) and
  `lib/java/pom.xml` (via `mvn versions:set`) **in CI**, then publishes.
- A `bump` job then commits that version back to `main`, so `main` always
  reflects the latest release.

Tags must be `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` (an optional pre-release suffix is
allowed); the `version` job fails on anything else. Releases are immutable per
version — pick a new tag to re-release.

## One-time setup

Repository secrets (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions):

- `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` — a crates.io API token with publish scope
  (https://crates.io/settings/tokens).
- `GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` — an armored GPG private key whose public key is on a
  keyserver (Central verifies the signatures).
- `GPG_PASSPHRASE` — that key's passphrase.
- `CENTRAL_USERNAME` / `CENTRAL_PASSWORD` — a Sonatype Central Portal **user
  token** (https://central.sonatype.com/account).

Also: `main` must be pushable by the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` (the `bump` job).
If `main` is protected, allow the Actions bot, or the bump step fails (after a
successful publish).

## Release

1. Create a **GitHub Release** on `main` tagged `vX.Y.Z` (publish it).
2. The workflow runs:
   - `version` — derive + validate `X.Y.Z` from the tag.
   - `rust` — set the version, test the publishable crates, publish them to
     crates.io in dependency order, upload the `.crate` files.
    - `java` — set the version, run `mvn -P release deploy` to Maven Central
      (auto-published after validation). The Java artifacts are pure JVM, so no
      per-platform native libs are staged.
    - `bump` — commit the version back to `main`.
    - `release-assets` — attach the `.crate` files and the Java main jars to the
      GitHub Release.

The Java deploy runs on **Maven 3.9.9** (pinned in the workflow): Maven 3.10
writes a `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
which the Portal rejects ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). The demos
are **excluded from the release reactor** (`-pl '!pathland-demo-views-kotlin,!pathland-desktop-demo,!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'`)
— `central-publishing-maven-plugin` bundles every reactor module, ignoring
`maven.deploy.skip`, and the demos must not be published.

The publish steps are **idempotent**: a crate+version already on crates.io is
skipped, so re-running a partially failed release is safe (re-run the workflow
via `workflow_dispatch`, passing the `tag`). Maven Central rejects a re-deploy of
an existing version, so a Java re-run only helps if the Java deploy did not
complete.

## Local pre-flight

Rust — `cargo publish --dry-run -p pathland-core` validates the leaf crate (the
dependent crates can only be dry-run once their dependencies are on crates.io,
so the ordered CI publish validates them).

Java — `mvn -P release verify` builds and signs the sources/javadoc jars without
uploading. It needs GPG installed and a `central` server in `~/.m2/settings.xml`:

```xml
<server>
  <id>central</id>
  <username>TOKEN_USERNAME</username>
  <password>TOKEN_PASSWORD</password>
</server>
```

## Publishable crates (dependency order)

```
pathland-core → pathland-markdown → pathland-engine → pathland-view → pathland-core-transport → pathland-render-html
```

(`pathland-view-native`, `pathland-core-capi`, `pathland-markdown-capi`,
`pathland-render-gtk`, `pathland-render-gtk-demo`, `pathland-html-golden`,
`pathland-ts-codegen` are **not** published — C-ABI cdylibs, the GTK renderer,
and dev tools.)

## Published Java modules

`pathland-view-core` (Kotlin JVM engine/SPI + the sole authoring DSL),
`pathland-render-html`, `pathland-server-core` (runtime, telemetry adapters,
Redis state store, and the shared WS test harness), `pathland-spring-boot-starter`,
`pathland-quarkus`, `pathland-quarkus-deployment` (plus the `pathland-parent`
POM). The demo modules (`pathland-demo-views-kotlin`, `pathland-desktop-demo`,
`pathland-quarkus-demo`, `pathland-spring-boot-demo`) set `maven.deploy.skip`.

state.output:
name: Release

# Publishing a GitHub Release (which creates the tag, e.g. `v0.1.1`) builds and
# publishes every artifact — the Rust crates to crates.io and the Java libraries
# to Maven Central (with the renderer's native libraries for every supported
# platform) — then attaches the built files to the Release.
#
# The tag drives the version: the workflow writes the tag's `X.Y.Z` into the Rust
# workspace version and the Java parent version (in CI only) before building, and
# a `bump` job commits that version back to `main` afterwards. No pre-bump commit
# is required. Tags must be `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` (an optional pre-release
# suffix is allowed).
#
# The publish steps are idempotent, so re-running a partially failed release is
# safe (a crate+version already on crates.io is skipped; Maven Central rejects a
# re-deploy of an existing version).
#
# Secrets:
#   CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN  crates.io API token (publish scope)
#   GPG_PRIVATE_KEY       armored GPG private key (signing)
#   GPG_PASSPHRASE        its passphrase
#   CENTRAL_USERNAME      Sonatype Central Portal user token username
#   CENTRAL_PASSWORD      Sonatype Central Portal user token password

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: 'Tag to release (e.g. v0.1.1); blank = current ref'
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  version:
    name: Resolve + validate version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      tag: ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
      version: ${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - id: v
        name: Derive the version from the tag
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          tag="${{ github.event.release.tag_name || inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}"
          if [[ ! "$tag" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::tag '$tag' must be v<major>.<minor>.<patch>"
            exit 1
          fi
          version="${tag#v}"
          echo "tag=$tag version=$version"
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  rust:
    name: Publish crates to crates.io
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: version
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Set the version from the tag
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cargo install cargo-edit --locked
          cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          # Sanity: the workspace version + the intra-workspace path-dep pins.
          awk -F'"' '/^version = /{print "workspace:", $2; exit}' Cargo.toml
          grep -rho 'pathland-[a-z-]*", version = "[^"]*"' crates/*/Cargo.toml | sort -u

      - name: Test the publishable crates
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo test -p pathland-core -p pathland-markdown -p pathland-engine -p pathland-view -p pathland-core-transport -p pathland-render-html

      - name: Publish in dependency order
        working-directory: lib/rust
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          crates=(pathland-core pathland-markdown pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html)
          for c in "${crates[@]}"; do
            echo "::group::publish $c $version"
            # Idempotent: skip a crate+version already on crates.io.
            if curl -sf -A "pathland-release-ci" "https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/$c/$version" >/dev/null; then
              echo "$c $version already published — skipping"
              echo "::endgroup::"
              continue
            fi
            # `cargo publish` packages (leaving the .crate in target/package) then uploads.
            # `--allow-dirty`: `cargo set-version` above intentionally edits the
            # crates' manifests (the path-dep version pins), so the tree is "dirty".
            cargo publish --allow-dirty -p "$c"
            echo "::endgroup::"
            # Let the index propagate so the next dependent crate resolves it.
            sleep 20
          done

      - name: Package (guarantee .crate files for the release assets)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # All dependencies are published by now, so packaging every crate works.
          for c in pathland-core pathland-markdown pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html; do
            cargo package --allow-dirty -p "$c"
          done

      - name: Upload the .crate files
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: crates
          path: lib/rust/target/package/*.crate
          if-no-files-found: error

  java:
    name: Publish to Maven Central
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [version]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}

      - name: Set up JDK + Maven credentials + GPG
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'
          cache: maven
          server-id: central
          server-username: CENTRAL_USERNAME
          server-password: CENTRAL_PASSWORD
          gpg-private-key: ${{ secrets.GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          gpg-passphrase: MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE

      # Maven 3.10 (the runner default since 2026-10-04) writes a
      # `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
      # which central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles and the Portal rejects
      # ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). 3.9.x does not. Pin it here.
      - name: Pin Maven 3.9.9
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          v=3.9.9
          curl -sSL "https://archive.apache.org/dist/maven/maven-3/$v/binaries/apache-maven-$v-bin.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$HOME"
          echo "$HOME/apache-maven-$v/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          mvn -v

      - name: Set the version from the tag
        working-directory: lib/java

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

          ref: main

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"

          distribution: temurin

metadata.output:
name: Release

# Publishing a GitHub Release (which creates the tag, e.g. `v0.1.1`) builds and
# publishes every artifact — the Rust crates to crates.io and the Java libraries
# to Maven Central (with the renderer's native libraries for every supported
# platform) — then attaches the built files to the Release.
#
# The tag drives the version: the workflow writes the tag's `X.Y.Z` into the Rust
# workspace version and the Java parent version (in CI only) before building, and
# a `bump` job commits that version back to `main` afterwards. No pre-bump commit
# is required. Tags must be `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` (an optional pre-release
# suffix is allowed).
#
# The publish steps are idempotent, so re-running a partially failed release is
# safe (a crate+version already on crates.io is skipped; Maven Central rejects a
# re-deploy of an existing version).
#
# Secrets:
#   CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN  crates.io API token (publish scope)
#   GPG_PRIVATE_KEY       armored GPG private key (signing)
#   GPG_PASSPHRASE        its passphrase
#   CENTRAL_USERNAME      Sonatype Central Portal user token username
#   CENTRAL_PASSWORD      Sonatype Central Portal user token password

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: 'Tag to release (e.g. v0.1.1); blank = current ref'
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  version:
    name: Resolve + validate version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      tag: ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
      version: ${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - id: v
        name: Derive the version from the tag
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          tag="${{ github.event.release.tag_name || inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}"
          if [[ ! "$tag" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::tag '$tag' must be v<major>.<minor>.<patch>"
            exit 1
          fi
          version="${tag#v}"
          echo "tag=$tag version=$version"
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  rust:
    name: Publish crates to crates.io
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: version
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Set the version from the tag
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cargo install cargo-edit --locked
          cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          # Sanity: the workspace version + the intra-workspace path-dep pins.
          awk -F'"' '/^version = /{print "workspace:", $2; exit}' Cargo.toml
          grep -rho 'pathland-[a-z-]*", version = "[^"]*"' crates/*/Cargo.toml | sort -u

      - name: Test the publishable crates
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo test -p pathland-core -p pathland-markdown -p pathland-engine -p pathland-view -p pathland-core-transport -p pathland-render-html

      - name: Publish in dependency order
        working-directory: lib/rust
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          crates=(pathland-core pathland-markdown pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html)
          for c in "${crates[@]}"; do
            echo "::group::publish $c $version"
            # Idempotent: skip a crate+version already on crates.io.
            if curl -sf -A "pathland-release-ci" "https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/$c/$version" >/dev/null; then
              echo "$c $version already published — skipping"
              echo "::endgroup::"
              continue
            fi
            # `cargo publish` packages (leaving the .crate in target/package) then uploads.
            # `--allow-dirty`: `cargo set-version` above intentionally edits the
            # crates' manifests (the path-dep version pins), so the tree is "dirty".
            cargo publish --allow-dirty -p "$c"
            echo "::endgroup::"
            # Let the index propagate so the next dependent crate resolves it.
            sleep 20
          done

      - name: Package (guarantee .crate files for the release assets)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # All dependencies are published by now, so packaging every crate works.
          for c in pathland-core pathland-markdown pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html; do
            cargo package --allow-dirty -p "$c"
          done

      - name: Upload the .crate files
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: crates
          path: lib/rust/target/package/*.crate
          if-no-files-found: error

  java:
    name: Publish to Maven Central
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [version]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}

      - name: Set up JDK + Maven credentials + GPG
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'
          cache: maven
          server-id: central
          server-username: CENTRAL_USERNAME
          server-password: CENTRAL_PASSWORD
          gpg-private-key: ${{ secrets.GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          gpg-passphrase: MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE

      # Maven 3.10 (the runner default since 2026-10-04) writes a
      # `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
      # which central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles and the Portal rejects
      # ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). 3.9.x does not. Pin it here.
      - name: Pin Maven 3.9.9
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          v=3.9.9
          curl -sSL "https://archive.apache.org/dist/maven/maven-3/$v/binaries/apache-maven-$v-bin.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$HOME"
          echo "$HOME/apache-maven-$v/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          mvn -v

      - name: Set the version from the tag
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true

      # The demos are excluded from the release reactor: central-publishing-maven-plugin
      # bundles every reactor module (it ignores maven.deploy.skip), and the demos must
      # not be published.
      - name: Deploy to Maven Central
        working-directory: lib/java
        env:
          CENTRAL_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_USERNAME }}
          CENTRAL_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_PASSWORD }}
          MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.GPG_PASSPHRASE }}
        run: >-
          mvn -B -P release deploy
          -pl '!pathland-demo-views-kotlin,!pathland-desktop-demo,!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'

      - name: Collect the published main jars
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist/jars
          for m in pathland-view-core pathland-render-html pathland-server-core \
                   pathland-spring-boot-starter pathland-quarkus \
                   pathland-quarkus-deployment; do
            cp lib/java/"$m"/target/"$m"-*.jar dist/jars/ 2>/dev/null || true
          done
          rm -f dist/jars/*-sources.jar dist/jars/*-javadoc.jar
          ls -la dist/jars

      - name: Upload the main jars
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: jars
          path: dist/jars/*.jar
          if-no-files-found: error

  bump:
    name: Commit the version back to main
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [version, rust, java]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - name: Set the Rust version
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cargo install cargo-edit --locked
          cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"

      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'
      - name: Set the Java version
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true

      - name: Commit + push
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          if git diff --quiet; then
            echo "version already current on main — nothing to commit"
            exit 0
          fi
          git add -A
          git commit -m "chore(release): v${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          git push origin HEAD:main

  release-assets:
    name: Attach release assets
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [version, rust, java]
    steps:
      - name: Download all build artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: dist

      - name: Collect the files to attach
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p out
          find dist -type f \( -name '*.crate' -o -name '*.jar' -o -name '*.dll' -o -name '*.so' -o -name '*.dylib' \) -exec cp {} out/ \;
          ls -la out

      - name: Attach to the GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: gh release upload "${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}" out/* --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --clobber

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
        <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
        <version>0.1.5</version>
    </parent>

    <artifactId>pathland-quarkus</artifactId>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>Pathland Quarkus</name>
    <description>
        Quarkus extension for Pathland: SSR at any path, live 16-byte opcode deltas over
        /ws, per-session state, plus the Kotlin authoring DSL. Add this extension and a
        PathlandApp bean and you have a running app. Author the root view with the Kotlin
        DSL in pathland-view-core; Java hosts mount Kotlin views.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-server-core</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view-core</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-kotlin</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-rest</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-websockets-next</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-micrometer</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-smallrye-health</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <!-- The OTel API is referenced only to build the optional tracing decorator; a
             Tracer bean exists only when the app adds quarkus-opentelemetry. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.opentelemetry</groupId>
            <artifactId>opentelemetry-api</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-junit5</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <!-- A registry backend so /q/metrics exists in the starter's tests. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-micrometer-registry-prometheus</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
            <artifactId>kotlin-stdlib</artifactId>
            <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>test-compile</id>
                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>test-compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                    <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
                <artifactId>quarkus-extension-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>extension-descriptor</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <capabilities>
                        <provides>dev.pathland.quarkus</provides>
                        <provides>dev.pathland.quarkus.kotlin</provides>
                    </capabilities>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"

    <parent>

        <version>0.1.5</version>
    </parent>

    <artifactId>pathland-quarkus-deployment</artifactId>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

        Build-time deployment module for the Pathland Quarkus extension, including the

        </dependency>

        </dependency>

        </dependency>
        <dependency>

# Welcome to the Quarkiverse Hub!

[](#welcome-to-the-quarkiverse-hub)

Quarkus is a Kubernetes Native Java stack tailored for the OpenJDK HotSpot and GraalVM, crafted from the best of breed Java libraries and standards, as well as an ever growing ecosystem of its extensions. At the beginning we were accepting all the contributed extensions in the core Quarkus repository. Eventually though it grew too large and lead to a maintenance overhead. In addition to that, in some cases it's simply not always sensible to include an extension into the main Quarkus repository. For example, an extension might want to have a release cadence which is independent of the core repository's lifecycle.

Quarkiverse is our solution to create a "home" for such extensions.

# What is Quarkiverse

[](#what-is-quarkiverse)

The [Quarkiverse GitHub organization](http://github.com/quarkiverse) provides repository hosting (including build, CI and release publishing setup) for Quarkus extension projects contributed by the community.

Quarkus extensions hosted in the Quarkiverse organization can easily be included into the Quarkus extensions catalog available on [code.quarkus.io](http://code.quarkus.io), [extensions.quarkus.io](http://extensions.quarkus.io), and the Quarkus command line tools (such as `mvn quarkus:list-extensions`, `gradle listExtensions`). To stay listed, the only requirement is that the extension keeps functioning, stays up-to-date and cause no harm.

# Why Quarkiverse

[](#why-quarkiverse)

In the early days and actually up until recently, Quarkus extensions contributed by the community members (including the core Quarkus team) have been welcomed in the main Quarkus repository at [https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus). Today the main repository has grown a lot and it's evident that it simply becomes troublesome to work with it for its contributors. That and other maintenance and infrastructure related issues inspired the creation of a separate organization called Quarkiverse to host Quarkus extension projects contributed by the community (including the Quarkus core team members themselves).

The advantages of joining Quarkiverse are:

-   Automated and secured publishing of your maven releases to Maven Central.
-   Automated Cross-testing of your extension with Quarkus builds/releases (see [https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-ecosystem-ci](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-ecosystem-ci))
-   Consistent formatting and release of project
-   Quarkus team members can in an emergency (i.e. maintainers are missing) help and fix issues.

Note: While the Quarkus project has the "keys" to publish under `io.quarkiverse`, each project in Quarkiverse is driven and maintained by the lead of that project. They decide what happens with the project - Quarkiverse will just expect releases to be compatible with Quarkus - if a project for some reason cannot do a release we can in the best scenario help or in the worst scenario we'll temporarily exclude the project from the affected registry entries to avoid end-users to have a bad experience.

If you do not want to commit to the above guidelines then you are more than welcome to publish an extension outside of Quarkus or Quarkiverse; and then you can still be listed in the registry - it is just not handled automatically. In this case we request you to use your own group ID to clearly identify those artifacts are from a third-party organization.

# Quarkiverse and Quarkus Platform

[](#quarkiverse-and-quarkus-platform)

The word Quarkiverse, derived from "Quarkus" and "universe", is carrying the meaning of the universe of Quarkus extensions. In other words, it is intended to represent a part of the Quarkus ecosystem. However, at the same time, there is also a notion of a Quarkus platform. There is a significant difference between the two.

While the extensions under the Quarkiverse organization are generally independent projects lead by independent development teams, the fundamental promise of a Quarkus platform is any combination of the Quarkus extensions the platform consists of can be used in the same application without causing any conflict for each other. Quarkus platform implies coordination, cross testing and dependency version alignment across extensions that constitute the platform which is not generally applicable to the Quarkiverse extensions. It is, however, still possible for extensions hosted in the Quarkiverse to join a Quarkus platform assuming they satisfy the purpose and policies defined for that platform.

# Joining Quarkiverse

[](#joining-quarkiverse)

## Getting an extension onboarded:

[](#getting-an-extension-onboarded)

See [ChecklistForNewProjects](checklistfornewprojects) for all the steps you'll need to start a new project in the Quarkiverse org.

The Quarkiverse team will provide the repository ready for development, nevertheless, it is always good to know that we respect the following conventions and policies.

## Documenting your extension

[](#documenting-your-extension)

All Quarkiverse extensions can include documentation on [http://docs.quarkiverse.io](http://docs.quarkiverse.io). See the [documentation about the documentation](documentingyourextension) for details on how how to document your extension.

## Managing settings on the GitHub repository

[](#managing-settings-on-the-github-repository)

Extension maintainers have full control over the repository settings, but be aware that the settings are infrastructure as code, managed with Terraform. To change any setting in the repository (give push permissions to anyone, enable a GitHub app, etc.), update the repository's `.tf` file. You may notice that, even as an extension maintainer, you have restricted permissions in the GitHub UI. This is to reduce the risk of accidents where maintainers make changes which then get overwritten by the next Terraform run.

## Expectations for Quarkiverse projects

[](#expectations-for-quarkiverse-projects)

Quarkiverse projects should follow some [naming conventions](namingconventions) for maven coordinates and package names.

### Identify Project Maintainer

[](#identify-project-maintainer)

Each project will have a GitHub team, and in here at least one must be listed and active as maintainer. This is the person that will be expected to lead and drive the project.

### Provide mechanism to do cross-testing of named quarkus core and platform versions

[](#provide-mechanism-to-do-cross-testing-of-named-quarkus-core-and-platform-versions)

All Quarkiverse projects should have a build and test suite that can be parameterized to use specific Quarkus and Platform versions to ensure we can get early warning of issues of master builds; but also to verify compatibility with maintenance branch/tags. This is handled by the [ecosystem CI](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-ecosystem-ci).

### Parent POM

[](#parent-pom)

All Quarkiverse projects are expected to use [io.quarkiverse:quarkiverse-parent](https://github.com/quarkiverse/quarkiverse-parent) as the parent POM. This POM contains common project release and artifact publishing configuration.

## LICENSE

[](#license)

The project is expected to be licensed under ASL 2.0.

## Discussions

[](#discussions)

[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions) are disabled by default in Quarkiverse extension repositories.

To avoid spreading information too much and make it hard to figure out where to post we have following default guidelines:

-   Development questions should be addressed in the [Mailing List](https://groups.google.com/g/quarkus-dev)
-   User questions in [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/quarkus) + the Quarkiverse project tag.

However we can enable it in the repository if the extension maintainer really wants it (open an issue requesting that and ping the `@quarkiverse/quarkiverse-owners` team in the issue). However be aware that Core developers will not follow or be aware of these discussions unless explicitly mentioned.

# Quarkus Extension Development Guides and References

[](#quarkus-extension-development-guides-and-references)

In case you need help creating a new Quarkus extension Maven project, please follow [Building My First Extension](https://quarkus.io/guides/building-my-first-extension) guide.

Other useful articles related to Quarkus extension development can be found under the [Writing Extensions](https://quarkus.io/guides/#writing-extensions) guide category on the [Quarkus.io](http://quarkus.io) website.

### Want to contribute to this Wiki?

[](#want-to-contribute-to-this-wiki)

[Fork it and send a pull request.](https://github.com/quarkiverse/quarkiverse)

parts.text:
Big finding: only pathland-parent POM is on Maven Central; the module artifacts (view-core, quarkus, etc.) are NOT. The release succeeded but apparently only the parent got deployed? Let's inspect the v0.1.5 Java job log to see. Possibly because modules don't inherit the release profile? Maven profiles are inherited; should be fine. Wait, `central-publishing-maven-plugin` with `<extensions>true</extensions>` builds a bundle at the root. Maybe the reactor's modules weren't included because... Let's check the log. This matters for the issue: what's actually broken.

Let me fetch the java job log.

input.command: gh run view 38445297171 --log 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'deploy|Deploying|central|error|warn|Reactor|pathland-quarkus|pathland-view-core' | head -120

Typically kotlin-maven-plugin compiles during `compile` phase, and javadoc:jar runs in `package`? Actually the error `package dev.pathland.view.core does not exist` suggests javadoc is only given Java sources (src/main/java) and not the compiled classpath? Javadoc's `@packages` option or sourcepath. The Java source Markdown.java references Kotlin classes; if Kotlin classes are compiled into target/classes first, javadoc should resolve via classpath. Unless the Kotlin compile happens in a later phase due to kotlin-maven-plugin config? Let's inspect pathland-view-core pom and the Markdown.java.

Need to research the issue and produce a plan (read-only). Goal: fix release javadoc failure and get Maven Central release working, plus Quarkiverse. The user provided error. Now the task is to plan the fix.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
        <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
        <version>0.1.5</version>
    </parent>

    <artifactId>pathland-view-core</artifactId>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>Pathland View</name>
    <description>
        The Pathland JVM engine, runtime and authoring DSL, written in Kotlin: the
        16-byte opcode protocol, retained-tree diff emitter, Angular-style signals,
        wire codec, router, state, lazy JNA ring interop, and the SwiftUI-shaped
        `dev.pathland.view.dsl` builders/modifiers every JVM host mounts. All server
        runtimes depend on this module. Runs on every LTS from Java 17.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
            <artifactId>kotlin-stdlib</artifactId>
            <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>net.java.dev.jna</groupId>
            <artifactId>jna</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>compile</id>
                        <phase>process-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/main/kotlin</sourceDir>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/main/java</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                    <execution>
                        <id>test-compile</id>
                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>test-compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</sourceDir>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/java</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                    <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                    <args>
                        <arg>-Xjvm-default=all</arg>
                    </args>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

parts.text:
Interesting: `kotlin:compile` ran but the compilation output... Did it actually compile? Between 12:02:15 and 12:02:36 (21s) - likely. But maybe Kotlin compile failed? No, javadoc started at 12:02:42. Test-compile at 12:02:36. Hmm, but `kotlin:test-compile` runs at process-test-sources, after compile. So main Kotlin compiled.

Why javadoc can't see it? Let's look at the `@options` file generated. Not in log. Possibly javadoc plugin computes classpath from `project.compileClasspathElements`, which includes target/classes. Hmm.

Wait, maybe the issue: `kotlin-maven-plugin` with sourceDirs including `src/main/java` compiles Markdown.java itself. Thus `dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown` is compiled by Kotlin compiler and exists in target/classes. Then javadoc re-processes only Java sources in src/main/java? And javadoc's default sourcepath may be src/main/java. It needs AttributedString in classpath. If target/classes is on classpath it should find.

But error "package dev.pathland.view.core does not exist" implies classpath doesn't include target/classes or the Kotlin classes weren't output there. Could the Kotlin compile output go elsewhere? Let's check local target/classes after a build. There's a target dir. Let's see if AttributedString.class exists.

Here is a checklist with the tasks to be performed on any new Quarkiverse extension repository:

# Requesting a new repository

[](#requesting-a-new-repository)

## [Create an `Extension Proposal` issue](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/new?assignees=&labels=kind%2Fextension-proposal&template=extension_proposal.yml) in the Quarkus repository

[](#create-an-extension-proposal-issue-in-the-quarkus-repository)

The core team can then decide if the extension should belong to core or as a Quarkiverse extension. Please indicate the lead maintainers for the extension, and preferably a URL with more information about the technology the extension should enable.

Once the lead maintainers are identified (their GitHub accounts), a pull-request is created in the [Quarkiverse DevOps repository](https://github.com/quarkiverse/quarkiverse-devops) with the data provided in a [`.tf` file](https://github.com/quarkiverse/quarkiverse-devops#workflow-for-new-repositories) (existing Quarkiverse members can do this without waiting for any Quarkiverse org owner).

❗ IMPORTANT

If you need to change any setting in the repository (give push permissions to anyone, enable a GitHub app, etc.), make sure you perform these changes in the repository's `.tf` file. Changes performed in the GitHub UI directly can be discarded at any time without notice. The GitHub Provider syntax can be found [here](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/integrations/github/latest/docs).

# Start coding

[](#start-coding)

When decided, the Quarkiverse Team will initialize the repository in the Quarkiverse organization for you with skeleton code ready. If you'd like to get started before then, you can start implementing your extension from a skeleton with this command:

mvn io.quarkus.platform:quarkus-maven-plugin:create-extension \\
 -DgroupId=io.quarkiverse.\[myext\] -DextensionId=\[my-ext\] -U

It's best not to create a Git repository, since migration of an existing repository into the Quarkiverse org can be complex.

## Set up your IDE's code format

[](#set-up-your-ides-code-format)

## Code format

[](#code-format)

Extensions generated with the `create-extension` goal of the Quarkus maven plugin expect code to be formatted according to the Quarkus conventions as documented in: [https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#ide-config-and-code-style](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#ide-config-and-code-style). The default CI setup will validate the format and fail your build if the files don't conform.

# After the repository is created

[](#after-the-repository-is-created)

## [Make your extension available in the tooling](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-extension-catalog#extensions)

[](#make-your-extension-available-in-the-tooling)

Most Quarkus extensions are listed in the [Quarkus community extension registry](https://quarkus.io/guides/extension-registry-user#registry.quarkus.io). Once extensions are included in the registry, they will be available on [code.quarkus.io](https://code.quarkus.io), [extensions.quarkus.io](https://extensions.quarkus.io), and in the Quarkus command line tools (such as `mvn quarkus:list-extensions`, `gradle listExtensions`).

A PR adding your extension to the catalog should be automatically created shortly after your first release. If it does not, you should add your extension manually. The community registry reads its contents from [quarkus-extension-catalog repository](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-extension-catalog/tree/main/extensions). To add your extension to catalog, create a `YAML` file with your extension's `group-id` and `artifact-id` in the [extensions directory of the quarkus-extension-catalog repository](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-extension-catalog/tree/main/extensions).

## [Allow your company to be named as a maintainer or contributor (optional)](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-extension-catalog#extensions)

[](#allow-your-company-to-be-named-as-a-maintainer-or-contributor-optional)

If you would like your company to be listed as a contributor or maintainer of the extension, register an opt in in the opt-in file in the [quarkus-extension-catalog repository](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-extension-catalog/blob/main/named-contributing-orgs-opt-in.yml).

## [Integrate with the Quarkus Ecosystem CI](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-ecosystem-ci#what-its-all-about)

[](#integrate-with-the-quarkus-ecosystem-ci)

If you wish to have your extension tested against the latest snapshot in Quarkus core, you need to register your extension in the Quarkus Ecosystem CI

url: https://github.com/quarkiverse/quarkus-<YOUR\_EXTENSION>
issues:
  repo: quarkiverse/quarkiverse
  latestCommit: <the issue number you created in the previous step>

### Repository name

[](#repository-name)

The repository name under the quarkiverse organization should have `quarkus-` prefix. This will help avoid potential conflicts when cloning and/or forking the repository.

### Project's Maven artifact `groupId`s

[](#projects-maven-artifact-groupids)

The Maven `groupId` of the project's artifacts should follow the following format: `io.quarkiverse.<project-name>`. In other words, the project’s `groupId` should start with the `io.quarkiverse.` prefix followed by the project-specific unique name (minus the `quarkus-` prefix) in which dots aren't allowed. Also, since your `groupId` should also be your root package name, if it contains characters that are not allowed in package names (such as `-`), you should concatenate all the parts of your project name to form a single, lowercased name. So if your repository is named `quarkus-foo-bar`, your `groupId` would become `io.quarkiverse.foobar`.

### Project's Maven artifact `artifactId`s

[](#projects-maven-artifact-artifactids)

The project’s `artifactId` should start with the `quarkus-` prefix.

### Root package name

[](#root-package-name)

The root package name is expected to be the same as the project’s Maven artifact `groupId`, i.e. `io.quarkiverse.jberet`, if project name is `jberet`. See the [`groupId` section](#projects-maven-artifact-groupids) for more details.

Now I understand Quarkiverse requirements. Need also documentation (docs/modules/ROOT/pages/index.adoc), quarkiverse-parent POM, groupId io.quarkiverse.pathland, repo quarkus-pathland. The extension currently depends on external dev.pathland artifacts, which is acceptable? Quarkiverse extension usually can depend on third-party libs published to Central. Yes.

But there's a nuance: Quarkiverse extensions are usually built in their own repo, not as part of Pathland monorepo. Migration of existing repo into Quarkiverse is complex. Options:
- A) Keep extension code in Pathland repo; request Quarkiverse hosting by moving just the two modules into a new quarkiverse/quarkus-pathland repo. Publishing of io.quarkiverse.* happens via Quarkiverse CI (JReleaser). This means duplicating/splitting code. 
- B) Publish under dev.pathland without joining Quarkiverse and instead register in the extension catalog (third-party group id allowed). But user explicitly wants Quarkiverse Hub.

Also there's a hard requirement: to publish under io.quarkiverse, the Quarkiverse org does the release with their credentials; you cannot publish io.quarkiverse from your own CI. So the plan must create the repo via the proposal process.

Maybe the user wants just create issues now, not implement. The initial request: "We need to create an issue for releasing maven artifacts to maven central. Also, in relation to that, we need to create and release quarkus extions for pathland to the Quarkiverse Hub!" Then they gave the current error. So the immediate plan is to fix the release and create the issues.

Given plan mode, we should deliver a plan. But we need to decide whether to actually fix the javadoc issue now. The user is mid-release and blocked. The plan should prioritize:

1. Fix javadoc failure in pathland-view-core.
2. Verify/publish to Maven Central, confirm artifacts.
3. Create issue(s) tracking.
4. Quarkiverse onboarding plan.

Let me determine the best javadoc fix. The root cause: Kotlin classes not resolved by javadoc because the Java source is compiled by Kotlin then maven-compiler, and javadoc doesn't see Kotlin classes. Wait, why? Let's dig more.

Let me think about maven-javadoc-plugin: It builds the classpath from `project.getCompileClasspathElements()`. That list includes `${project.build.outputDirectory}` (target/classes) as the FIRST element, then dependencies. So target/classes is on classpath. So Kotlin classes should resolve. Unless the plugin uses `-sourcepath` and with `-sourcepath` set to `src/main/java`, and when javadoc finds the imported package not in sourcepath, it looks at classpath. It should.

But: The `Markdown.java` imports `dev.pathland.view.core.AttributedString`. Kotlin compiler compiled it into target/classes/dev/pathland/view/core/AttributedString.class. So fine.

Unless the Java file was compiled by kotlin compiler but the Kotlin compile step FAILED to emit because there were errors? No, test-compile ran.

Wait — maybe pathland-view-core's Kotlin compilation in the release CI was skipped or output to a different directory because the kotlin-maven-plugin's `output` default? No, target/classes.

Hmm, but local target/classes has AttributedString.class. Could be from before refactor (old) or from a local Maven build.

Let me look at the actual `@options` in the GitHub Actions run if javadoc prints it at debug. Not available.

Maybe the issue is simpler: `javadoc` fails for Kotlin-defined types even if classpath has them because javadoc is invoked with `@packages` (the source packages) and `-sourcepath src/main/java`; the import `dev.pathland.view.core` is not in sourcepath. Javadoc searches sourcepath for source files of imported packages; if absent, it consults classpath. It should find .class. Known behavior: javadoc can resolve types from class files on classpath. Yes.

Let me check whether the classpath actually includes target/classes by looking at javadoc plugin's `@options` in a local run... prohibited (writes). Could we run javadoc in a temp dir outside workspace? Plan mode says no changes to system; running a build in temp writes files, still a change but to temp. The instructions: "STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: ANY file edits, modifications, or system changes. Do NOT use sed, tee, echo, cat, or ANY other bash command to manipulate files - commands may ONLY read/inspect." So we can't run a build. We can only reason.

Let's search the web for this exact error pattern with Kotlin/javadoc.

Actually, I recall the real reason now: maven-javadoc-plugin 3.6.3's `jar` goal by default calls javadoc with `<sourcepath>` set to all source roots, but Maven's project has only `src/main/java` as a compile source root (Kotlin plugin doesn't add `src/main/kotlin` as a Java source root maybe). Then javadoc runs on the Java file. The classpath `${project.compileClasspathElements}` does include target/classes? Let me verify: In Maven, `project.getCompileClasspathElements()` returns `${project.build.outputDirectory}` plus compile dependencies. Yes it does.

Could the problem be that target/classes is NOT yet populated because Kotlin compile is bound to `process-sources`, which is BEFORE `compile`, but it is populated. Then maven-compiler at compile compiles Markdown.java. So populated.

Yet javadoc says package does not exist. Maybe javadoc plugin excludes target/classes when it equals the destination? No.

Wait — the error was on `pathland-view-core`, and the javadoc command was `javadoc @options @packages`. Could it be that the classpath entry for target/classes is present but javadoc's `-sourcepath` includes target/generated-sources/... and it uses `-subpackages`? Not sure.

Let's look at GitHub issue: "Kotlin classes not found by javadoc". Common solution is to bind kotlin compile BEFORE maven-compiler and make javadoc run after. Already.

Alternatively, the simplest robust fix: since javadoc can't process Kotlin anyway, skip javadoc generation and attach an empty javadoc jar. Central requires sources+javadoc jars for each artifact. An empty javadoc jar is accepted. Many Kotlin projects do this. Quarkiverse uses JReleaser which can publish without javadoc? Central requires javadoc jar.

But better: use Dokka to generate javadoc jars for Kotlin modules and maven-javadoc for pure Java modules. That's heavier.

Another approach: use `<sourcepath>` with the Java dir only and add `<classpath>`? Or use `<additionalJOption>`? Hmm.

Wait, maybe the actual cause is different: The `Markdown.java` file is under `src/main/java`, but the Kotlin plugin is configured with `<sourceDirs>` including both `src/main/kotlin` and `src/main/java`, and the Kotlin plugin may *not* be running under `mvn` because `kotlin-maven-plugin` uses daemon? No.

Let me check the annotation: `AttributedString` class is Kotlin with a private constructor and companion. Javadoc needs to load the class. It exists.

Could the issue be that javadoc is invoked with `--release 17` and the Kotlin classes were compiled for a newer bytecode (jvmTarget 17, fine).

Let me consider that target/classes was cleaned? The release workflow checks out tag and runs `mvn deploy` (no clean). target/classes may be absent at javadoc time if Kotlin compile output went somewhere else. But kotlin plugin creates it.

Hmm, what if `kotlin-maven-plugin` 2.4.10 with `jvmTarget=17` compiles to `target/classes`, and the maven-compiler-plugin default-compile also runs and *cleans*? No.

Let me check what the local pathland-view-core jar contains: presumably includes Markdown.class and AttributedString.class. Yes.

Perhaps the real reason is a known incompatibility: javadoc does not read classes that are in the *project's own output directory* because the plugin deliberately removes it to avoid doclet self-reference? I doubt.

Let me search the web quickly for "maven-javadoc-plugin kotlin package does not exist target/classes". Use websearch.

The problem is not in your maven configuration.
You need to include a package-info.java for the utils package.
It is a file located at src/main/java/utils/package-info.java that will contain the javadoc for the package, in contrast to the javadoc for a class.
For more information about package-level javadocs, you can read the documentation .

parts.text:
`pathland-render-core` has `publish = false`, but `pathland-core-transport` (publishable) depends on it by path+version. That's the bug: a publishable crate cannot depend on an unpublished crate. Need to either:
- Make `pathland-render-core` publishable (remove `publish = false`, add to publish order), or
- Remove the dependency from core-transport (if only dev/test), or
- Mark the dependency as not published? Cargo requires all non-dev dependencies be on crates.io.

Let's see why core-transport depends on render-core. Maybe for decode support. Let's inspect. If it's a real runtime dependency, publish render-core. But render-core also depends on engine/view, so publish order: core → markdown → engine → view → render-core → core-transport → render-html. That seems natural. So the plan should make `pathland-render-core` publishable (remove publish=false) and add it to the workflow's list/order. But is render-core intended to be private? AGENTS says render-core is a shared toolkit-free crate; could be published. Let's check its README/description and whether it has `publish = false` intentionally. `pathland-render-gtk` (also publish=false) depends on it. Publishing render-core is fine.

But wait, `pathland-core-transport` depends on `pathland-render-core`; if render-core remains unpublished, the release will always fail. This is a new regression from recent refactor. We should include it in the plan (likely as part of the Maven/release issue or a separate bug).

Also check for other publishable crates with path deps on unpublished crates. Let's enumerate publishable crates and their path deps:
- pathland-core: none.
- pathland-markdown: core (published).
- pathland-engine: core, markdown (published).
- pathland-view: core, engine, markdown.
- pathland-core-transport: core, engine, view, render-core (NOT published).
- pathland-render-html: core, core-transport.
Potential others: `pathland-ts-codegen` (no publish=false but dev tool, should be excluded), `pathland-engine-golden` (dev), `pathland-protocol-manifest` (dev). The workflow list excludes them.

So two blockers:
1. Rust: add pathland-render-core to publish list/order (or remove dep).
2. Java: javadoc fails on pathland-view-core.

Now, the user's request was to create an issue for "releasing maven artifacts to maven central" and "create and release quarkus extensions for pathland to the Quarkiverse Hub". Given the discovered blockers, the issue(s) should capture:
- Release pipeline currently broken (both ecosystems) — fix Rust publish order and Java javadoc, re-release.
- Maven Central module publication.
- Quarkiverse onboarding.

I think the best deliverable now is a plan with:
A. Create two GitHub issues (with drafted bodies).
B. Fix release blockers.
C. Re-release.
D. Quarkiverse onboarding (create proposal issue externally, etc.).

But since plan mode, we need approval. We should ask clarifying questions:
1. Issue granularity: one tracking issue vs three (release fix, Maven Central, Quarkiverse).
2. Javadoc approach.
3. Quarkiverse migration approach.

Let me also verify the current CI workflow to know what tests run (ci.yml) so the plan includes updating CI. And check docs. Maybe not needed.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, 'docs/**', 'feature/**', 'fix/**', 'refactor/**', 'spec/**']
  pull_request:

jobs:
  design:
    name: Design (Style Dictionary)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: design/package-lock.json

      # Build the generated token CSS / manifest / bundle and validate the
      # three token layers against the protocol catalog, dark/forced-dark
      # rules, and the canonical length conventions.
      - name: Install, build, check
        working-directory: design
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run build
          npm run check

      # The Rust renderer embeds the generated bundle (committed for packaging).
      - name: Verify the committed renderer CSS matches the design build
        run: scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check

  rust:
    name: Rust (workspace + C ABI + no_std/wasm)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [design]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # The workspace includes pathland-render-gtk (GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer)
      # and pathland-render-qt (Qt Quick), so the runner needs the GTK4,
      # libadwaita, GStreamer, and Qt system libraries before `cargo test` can
      # link them. GStreamer is required because the GTK renderer plays app-driven
      # media through a direct GStreamer playbin (GTK4's own media backend is
      # compiled out of some builds); the plugins are the runtime set the audio
      # stack uses (playbin, volume/audioconvert, mp3 decode). The Qt libraries
      # are installed in the next step.
      - name: Install GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libgtk-4-dev \
            libadwaita-1-dev \
            libglib2.0-dev \
            libcairo2-dev \
            libpango1.0-dev \
            libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-dev \
            libgraphene-1.0-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev \
            gstreamer1.0-plugins-base \
            gstreamer1.0-plugins-good \
            gstreamer1.0-libav

      - name: Install Qt6 (QML/Quick) system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            qt6-base-dev \
            qt6-declarative-dev \
            qt6-declarative-private-dev \
            qt6-multimedia-dev \
            qml6-module-qtqml \
            qml6-module-qtqml-models \
            qml6-module-qtqml-workerscript \
            qml6-module-qtquick \
            qml6-module-qtquick-layouts \
            qml6-module-qtquick-controls \
            qml6-module-qtquick-templates \
            qml6-module-qtquick-window \
            qml6-module-qtmultimedia
        # The dev headers alone don't ship the QML runtime modules; the Qt
        # renderer's offscreen tests instantiate the QML (QtQml + WorkerScript,
        # Items, stacks/Grid via QtQuick.Layouts, Qt Quick Controls, Multimedia)
        # through QQmlComponent, so the qml6-module-* runtime files are required
        # too. Note the Qt6 package names: `-window` (the Qt5 `-window2` name
        # does not exist), and private headers need qt6-declarative-private-dev.

      - name: Install Rust (stable + wasm32 target)
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown

      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: lib/rust -> target

      - name: Test workspace
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo test

      - name: Qt renderer headless smoke
        working-directory: lib/rust
        env:
          QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
          QT_QUICK_BACKEND: software
        run: cargo test -p pathland-render-qt

      # The DOM renderer's constants/token conventions and the cross-renderer SSR
      # golden fixtures are GENERATED from Rust (pathland-ts-codegen /
      # pathland-html-golden). Regenerate them here and fail if the committed
      # files drifted — so a renumbered constant or a changed SSR shape can't land
      # without its TS/fixture counterparts.
      - name: Verify generated TS + golden fixtures are current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen
          cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit
          git diff --exit-code -- \
            lib/typescript/src/constants.ts \
            lib/typescript/src/generated \
            lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr

      # The neutral protocol manifest is the machine-readable mirror consumed by
      # non-Rust bindings. Regenerate it from the canonical Rust constants and fail
      # if the committed `spec/protocol.tsv` drifted. The Java job validates its
      # hand-written constants against this file.
      - name: Verify the protocol manifest is current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest
          git -C ../.. diff --exit-code -- spec/protocol.tsv

      # The shared engine traces are emitted by the canonical Rust engine and
      # compared byte-for-byte by the JVM engine test. Verify the committed
      # fixtures have not drifted from the current engine behavior.
      - name: Verify engine trace fixtures are current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --check

      - name: Build the C ABI (cdylib, used by the Java JNA ring interop / native hosts)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-core-capi

      - name: no_std / wasm32 direction guard
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: ./check-wasm.sh

  java:
    name: Java (Maven reactor, JDK ${{ matrix.java }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [rust]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        java: ['17', '21', '25']
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Whole-stack floor is Java 17 (maven.compiler.release=17; JNA native binding,
      # thread-local environment); the matrix proves every LTS from 17.
      - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java }}
          cache: maven

      - name: Test reactor (incl. the SSR web demos)
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -q -B test

      # Mirror the Dockerfile's Maven selection so the deploy image path is
      # exercised in CI. The deployment module must be selected explicitly: it is
      # not a Maven dependency of the demo, and the runtime extension descriptor
      # validates against it.
      - name: Package the deployable Quarkus demo
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: >-
          mvn -q -B
          -pl pathland-quarkus-demo,pathland-quarkus-deployment -am
          package -Dmaven.test.skip=true

  web-client:
    name: Web client (TypeScript DOM renderer)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: lib/typescript/package-lock.json

      - name: Install, typecheck, test, build
